name: java-springboot
description: 'Get best practices for developing applications with Spring Boot.'

Build: Use Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle`) for dependency management. Use Spring Boot starters (e.g., `spring-boot-starter-web`, `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`).
Structure: Organize by feature/domain (e.g., `com.example.app.order`, `com.example.app.user`), not layer (e.g., `com.example.app.controller`, `com.example.app.service`).
Always use constructor-based injection for required dependencies. This makes components easier to test and dependencies explicit. Declare dependency fields `private final`.
Use `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, and `<REDACTED_USER>`/`<REDACTED_USER>` annotations appropriately to define beans.
Configuration: Use `application.yml` (or `application.properties`); YAML is often preferred for readability and hierarchical structure. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` for strongly-typed configuration. Use Spring Profiles (`application-dev.yml`, `application-prod.yml`) for environment-specific configuration.
Do not hardcode secrets. Use environment variables, or a dedicated secret management tool like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager.
APIs: Design clear, consistent RESTful endpoints. Use DTOs in the API layer. Do not expose JPA entities directly to the client. Validate request DTOs with Java Bean Validation (JSR 380) annotations (`<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`).
